assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built a systematic, formal and empirically testable framework for how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It has reshaped political economics and links institutions to policy outcomes. Influence on both theory and empirical work is broad.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the core pairing, with the work developed through their joint book and papers. Besley's work with Persson on state capacity and fiscal capacity is a distinct and well-documented complement, so a three-person award is defensible. Other contributors to the political-economy literature are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s onward and has been tested and extended for decades. It is old enough to have broad confirmation, though the 2024 institutions prize may reduce the appetite for a nearby topic.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the recent institutions and growth prize in the committee's view of balance.
Some causal empirical claims about electoral rules are contested.
Whether the committee prefers a pair or a trio is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity model of trade changed the unit of analysis from the industry to the firm. It explains selection into exporting, reallocation, and a new channel for the gains from trade, and it underpins a great deal of empirical trade work with firm-level data. The influence is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution. Helpman's role is substantial through Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple and the later extensive-margin work. Redding is an important extender but is less clearly foundational. Bernard and Jensen's empirical groundwork is not credited on this ballot, which is a gap.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation and refinement, with a very large empirical literature. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernard and Jensen weakens the attribution picture.
Krugman's 2008 prize on new trade theory may be seen as partly overlapping.
Helpman's other work could be counted under a different ballot entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, together with rule-based monetary policy analysis, is the dominant paradigm in central-bank practice and in macroeconomic teaching. Practical influence on policy is very large, and the theoretical coherence is high.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. The framework was built by many hands: Calvo (pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts), Woodford and Gali (the canonical formulation), and Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others (medium-scale estimation). Any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of application. Its performance in the 2021-22 inflation episode is a partial and ongoing test.
uncertainties: Crowded attribution may make a three-name award unconvincing.
The choice among Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali and the estimation group is contestable.
Rigid-price microfoundations remain debated empirically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Used population-scale administrative data to measure intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run returns to policy. It shifted both public debate and academic practice toward credible, register-based measurement. It fits the tradition of credible quasi-experimental and register-data evidence well, and the measurement is replicable.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader. Hendren's work on neighbourhood effects and Friedman's on tax-record mobility and teacher value-added are strong contributions, but the group is a research team and the marginal credit among members is hard to separate. Katz's earlier Moving to Opportunity work is also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Most of the work dates from the 2010s onward, so it is comparatively young. Replication of key findings is encouraging, but some policy conclusions, such as neighbourhood effects and value-added, are still debated.
uncertainties: Relatively short track record for the most-cited results.
Credit shared between the Chetty group and Katz and other earlier researchers.
Data access limits independent replication.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock studies documented the local labour-market costs of rapid import competition. The task-based approach to technology reshaped how economists understand automation, polarization and wage inequality. Both strands changed policy debates on trade adjustment and technological change.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Hanson both link the trade-shock and technology agendas, and Autor leads on the task framework. Dorn is a key co-author on the trade work. Katz's role belongs mainly to the earlier skill-premium literature, where Goldin and Katz have already been recognized, with Goldin's 2023 prize.
assessment.maturity: The papers date from 2003 (tasks) and 2013 (China shock). The follow-up literature is large, though results on persistence and magnitudes are still being updated.
uncertainties: Identification of the China shock and its quantitative magnitudes are debated.
Overlap with the Goldin-Katz skill-biased technical change literature, already honoured.
Whether Dorn and Acemoglu-Restrepo should share credit on tasks and automation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's alternating-offers model (1982) gave bargaining a tractable non-cooperative foundation with a unique subgame-perfect solution. The market-bargaining extensions with Wolinsky link search and bargaining and underpin wage-setting and matching models. The conceptual contribution is deep and widely taught.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the clear originator. Wolinsky is credited for the markets and decentralized-trade extensions. Binmore's role in the early analysis and in the Nash programme is also significant, and Stahl's earlier related result is not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use across fields, which is firmly mature. It is probably already a standard, and the tradeoff is age against the recent preference for applied results.
uncertainties: Game theory has been recognized often, so the field balance may weigh against it.
The right set of co-laureates (Wolinsky versus Binmore) is unclear.
Applied relevance is indirect, mainly through search and wage models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints interact with asset prices to amplify and propagate shocks. This is a core mechanism for understanding credit cycles and financial crises, and it underlies much macro-financial modelling after 2008.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore is a clean two-person original contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist add the financial-accelerator tradition, which builds on Bernanke-Gertler and where Bernanke was already recognized in 2022. Gertler also appears in the New Keynesian ballot.
assessment.maturity: The theory is nearly thirty years old and was tested heavily in and after the 2008 crisis. Empirical identification of the mechanism is more mixed than the theory's influence suggests.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may crowd out this topic.
Direct empirical confirmation of collateral amplification is partial.
Boundary with the Gertler contributions to other lines of work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion offers a clean, widely applicable account of how a sender designs information to influence a decision-maker, and it launched the information design literature. It is conceptually elegant and has applications in markets, regulation and communication.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow (2011) are the originators. Bergemann and Morris developed information design and robust predictions in parallel and are central to the field's breadth. Choosing between these pairs is a real attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years old, which is young by committee standards. Applications are growing but empirical validation remains limited.
uncertainties: Too recent for a clear verdict on lasting influence.
Contested split of credit between Kamenica-Gentzkow and Bergemann-Morris.
Limited direct empirical confirmation compared with other candidates.
